t: This is KOKO in Camden Town, a music venue that began life as a theatre. It opened in 1900 as the Camden Theatre, became a variety house in 1909, and a cinema two years later. After the war the BBC took it over and stayed until 1972. It reopened in 1977 as The Music Machine, then became the Camden Palace in 1982. After a major restoration from 2004, it was renamed Koko. The architect was W. G. R. Sprague, a pupil of Frank Matcham, who designed at least thirty-five theatres between 1890 and 1929.
